diagnosis:
The scenario has two distinct failure modes: (1) check C8 fails in 3 of 4 rollouts (rollouts 0, 1, 2) despite PF3 being revealed and cited in every settled case — this is an ENCODING MISMATCH; (2) rollout 3 auto-failed on the turn cap at 18 turns without settling — this is a STRUCTURAL problem with the settle-eligibility condition.

**C8 (ENCODED MISMATCH, rollouts 0, 1, 2):** In all three settled rollouts, PF3 was revealed by A4 and cited in justification_fact_ids. The settlement's evaluation_gate value is 'task success of at least 85% on a manually sampled set of exactly 40 review tasks' and rollout_approved is set (true in rollout 0, false in rollouts 1 and 2). C7 and C9 — which also gate on PF3 — pass in all three rollouts, confirming the fact was properly surfaced and used. C8 is the sole PF3-linked check that fails, and it fails consistently regardless of whether rollout_approved is true or false. This pattern indicates C8's wording or threshold does not match how the model naturally encodes the 'approval remains withheld until revision is complete' requirement from PF3. The fact states approval should remain withheld until the evaluation gate revision is complete; rollouts 1 and 2 withhold approval (rollout_approved=false) with commitments to complete the revision, yet C8 still fails. The check appears to expect a specific encoding (e.g., an exact field name or a specific boolean/commitment structure) that the model's settlement format does not produce.

**Rollout 3 (STRUCTURAL — settle-eligibility):** Rollout 3 hit the turn cap at 18 turns without settling. All three decisive facts (PF1, PF2, PF3) were revealed by turn 7. By turn 15, all three fact-holders confirmed their revisions were posted. Turns 16 and 17 are other agents urging A1 to approve. A1 never issues a settle action. This is not a pacing problem — 18 turns is more than sufficient for four agents to each reveal and confirm. The problem is that A1's settle-eligibility condition (per shared_context: 'cannot approve until every required policy revision is confirmed in the rollout ticket and all required launch documentation is attached') is being interpreted too strictly: A1 waits for explicit confirmation from every agent but never triggers a settle even after all confirmations are in. The condition needs loosening so that A1 can settle once all facts are revealed and acknowledged, rather than requiring a rigid confirmation round that A1 may never initiate.
